items.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: One of the, if not the best band that I have ever worked with was the Basie band. Count Basie’s band swings like no other band ever.

ctx.x: How is your — I know that you and Joe Williams go back quite a ways.

Joe is new with John Levy. He’s only been with him maybe fifteen or twenty years. One of the, if not the best band that I have ever worked with was the Basie band. Count Basie’s band swings like no other band ever. There just was never a band like that. Joe Williams was, at that time when Joe Williams was with the Basie band, I mean it didn’t get any better than Joe Williams and the Basie band. I love the ballads that Joe sings today but I really love the energy that was there with the Basie band. Joe Williams…
We’ve talked to a good number of Basie alumnus and from other groups too.

items.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Your dad had a Victrola, right?

Oh yeah. We played – he listened to Count Basie. In fact I heard Little Jimmy Scott with – Lionel Hampton, wasn’t it? So I had to be maybe 10, then. But he would listen. And the Ink Spots. I remember he loved the Ink Spots. So basically Daddy was the one who listened to music.
